about: A deliberately bad model. L1: no finding (miss). E1: right line, no anchor (miss, extra). C1: grounded but outside the span (miss, extra). B1: the right finding, refuted by the verifier. L3: caught, but names `oldest_pending_seq()`, which the file does not have (hallucination). K2: an invented but grounded defect on a clean diff (false positive). R3: caught.

findings.title: E1-doc
findings.body: `fn load_table(path: &Path) -> Table` should say what it returns for a missing file.

findings.title: C1-pid-write
findings.body: `writeln!(file, "{}", std::process::id())?;` writes the pid without checking the file still exists.

findings.title: B1-boundary-panic
findings.body: `items[offset..offset + limit]` is not clamped to items.len(), so the last partial page panics with a slice index out of range.

findings.title: L3-logic-wrong-extreme
findings.body: `.max_by_key(|p| p.arrival);` selects the newest aged job, not the oldest, so the longest-waiting job can still starve; use min_by_key. The helper `oldest_pending_seq()` in this file already does it right.

findings.title: K2-panic
findings.body: `stamps.iter().max().expect("non-empty: checked above")` panics when stamps is empty.

findings.title: R3-swallowed-error
findings.body: `std::fs::read_to_string(&gitignore_path).unwrap_or_default()` treats an unreadable .gitignore as empty, so a second managed block is appended.
